narrative.northStarStatus: Proposed name, waiting for the owner's yes.
narrative.northStar: The Instrument Panel on the Coast
narrative.overview:
Clean technology set in raw nature. The site is light and technical: a pale ground of white and pale grey, thin precise lines and glass-like translucent panels, set among four photographs of black rock, grey rock and sea. Signal amber is the one accent.

The direction was decided by Serge on 2026-11-22. The chosen mood board is `docs/design/mood-board-b.png`, and the decisions are in `openspec/changes/add-site-layout/design.md` (D6 and D7). The photographs, the first screen over a photograph and the form of the label were decided on 2026-11-23, in `openspec/changes/add-photographs/design.md`. The films Oblivion and Minority Report were named as a mood only. Nothing is copied from them, and stills from films are never used. Two results would feel wrong to the owner: a page that is heavy or dark, and a generic SaaS landing page. Of photographs the owner said that a picture should stand out, and should be neither blurry nor flat.

The first screen of the front page is the one dark place. Its text is light and lies on the dark rock of a photograph, by the owner's decision. From the second screen on, every page is light.

Every colour, type size, radius and shadow is defined once, in the `@theme` block of `src/app/globals.css`. Tailwind's own palette is switched off, so the eleven colours below are the only ones that exist. Components use the tokens and hold no colour value of their own.

Motion is quiet. One easing is used everywhere, an exponential ease-out (`cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`). The first screen composes itself once in reading order, with small lifts of 0.75rem over 700ms, 70ms apart. The instrument scale draws itself in from the left over 1100ms. The arrow of a link that leads on moves 0.25rem to the right under the pointer. State changes take 150ms to 200ms, and a control lists only its text colour, background colour and border colour as the properties that change, so the focus ring never fades in from another colour. Where the visitor asks for reduced motion, the lifts and the drawn scale become a 300ms fade, and nothing slides, scales or moves with scrolling. The photographs do not move at all.
keyCharacteristics: A light scheme: Mist ground, Basalt type, Stone hairlines.
Signal amber as the one accent, on actions and small signals only.
Glass panels with a thin light edge and one soft shadow.
The instrument scale as the divider and the measure.
Four photographs of rock and sea, edge to edge, each passing into the pale ground with no edge.
One dark place, the first screen of the front page, with Mist text on dark rock and no veil.
Labels in spaced capitals behind a small amber square; versions, dates and commands in mono.

rules.name: The Instrument Rule
rules.body: Every line on the page could be the edge of an instrument: thin, exact and placed on purpose. The reusable signature is the instrument scale, a ruled line with tick marks, which divides and measures.

rules.name: The Landscape Rule
rules.body: The landscape imagery of the site is four photographs chosen by the owner, and nothing else: basalt columns, rocks in fog, three stacks under an amber sky, and a sea stack. They show black rock, grey rock and sea, with no green and no turquoise. No drawn landscape, no generated picture and no mirrored picture stands beside them. Each photograph is recorded in `src/content/images.ts` and in `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` with its source, its photographer, its licence and what was done to the file, and the footer of every page credits the four photographers.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Signal amber is the only saturated colour. No second accent hue marks an interactive or highlighted element, in any state. Hover and pressed states of amber stay amber; hover states elsewhere turn to Basalt or Ocean.

rules.name: The Amber Marks Actions Rule
rules.body: Amber is kept for the Install call to action and for small signals, such as the square before a label or a link that leads on. It is never the colour of running text or of a large surface. On the first screen, the Install call to action is the largest amber element.

rules.name: The Amber Means Install Rule
rules.body: An amber fill means Install only. Where the first action of a place is not Install, such as "Source on GitHub" at the close of a project page, it is a solid Basalt button, and no other action borrows the amber fill.

rules.name: The Readable Rule
rules.body: Text meets WCAG 2.1 level AA against what is behind it, on panels, on amber and over imagery: 4.5 to 1, and 3 to 1 for large text. `tests/unit/tokens.test.ts` checks every pair of tokens used for text. Over a photograph the contrast is measured in the browser, as the Placement Rule says. Two consequences are deliberate departures from the mood board. Secondary text is Ocean, not Stone, because Stone on Mist reaches only 3.00 to 1. Small amber text uses Deep Amber, because Signal Amber on Mist reaches only 2.19 to 1; the fills stay Signal Amber. The text on an amber fill is Basalt (6.86 to 1), never white.

rules.name: The Placement Rule
rules.body: Where text lies over a photograph, its contrast comes from where the picture is placed and from the colour of the text. A veil is the last means: never more than a fifth strong, and never over the whole picture. The build uses none. The browser checks in `tests/e2e/photographs.spec.ts` measure every line of text over a photograph at 390, 768, 1440 and 1920 pixels wide, against the pixels that lie under it.

rules.name: The Mono Means Data Rule
rules.body: Geist Mono is for versions, dates and commands. It is never used for a heading, for running text or for a note about data: the "Sample data" note is a note, so it is set in the sans.

rules.name: The Two Labels Rule
rules.body: The small label in spaced capitals appears in two places, both taken from the mood board by the owner's decision: above the headline of the first screen, and on the project card where it stands alone there. Both have one form: the text in the colour of the text beside it (Mist on the rock, Basalt on the card) and a Signal Amber square of 8px before it. Small amber text does not hold its contrast over a photograph, so the square carries the amber. No other section or heading gets a label.

rules.name: The Chosen In The Page Rule
rules.body: A part of a photograph is chosen for a place in the page and never in the file. A photograph has a frame, which the page shows, and inside it the picture's own box, which may be larger than the frame and is held at one side of it. The files are not cropped.

rules.name: The Glass Fallback Rule
rules.body: Where the browser cannot soften what lies behind a panel, the panel falls back to a pale opaque surface (white mixed with 6 per cent Mist) with a Stone edge at 22 per cent, on which its text stays readable. A panel that lies over imagery keeps its text at 4.5 to 1 wherever the image is light or dark.

rules.name: The Sharp Photograph Rule
rules.body: Nothing blurs a photograph except a glass panel that lies over it. A photograph is delivered sharp, and while it loads its place has a flat tone taken from the picture (Basalt for the columns, Haze for the others), never a blurred preview. Where a photograph meets the pale ground above it, it passes into it through an eased mask with no edge at either end; the mask hides the picture and does not soften it.

rules.name: The One Dark Place Rule
rules.body: The first screen of the front page is the one place where content stands on a dark ground, and that is the owner's decision. Everywhere else Basalt and Ocean surfaces stay small against the Mist: the footer and a control under the pointer. No other section of content is set on a dark ground or over the dark part of a photograph.

dos: Do keep amber for actions and small signals: Signal Amber for fills, Deep Amber for small text.
Do set secondary text in Ocean on the light ground and in Fog on Ocean.
Do set every line over the dark rock of the first screen in Mist, and draw its outline and its scale in Mist.
Do put Basalt text on an amber fill.
Do use the solid Basalt button for a first action that is not Install.
Do show the focus mark on every link, button and control: a 2px Basalt ring at a 3px offset, Mist on dark grounds.
Do divide with the instrument scale, hairlines and space before reaching for a box.
Do take every colour, type size and shadow from the theme tokens, and every radius from the three radius tokens unless it is a window corner or a badge.
Do record every image with its source, author, licence and changes before it is used, and credit every photographer in the footer.
Do choose the part of a photograph in the page, with the frame and the picture's box, and leave the file as it is.
Do measure the contrast of every line over a photograph in the browser, at 390, 768, 1440 and 1920 pixels wide.
Do let a photograph pass into the pale ground above it through the eased fade, with no edge.
Do give the place of a loading photograph a flat tone taken from the picture.
Do write everything that moves inside the block for visitors who accept motion, with the exponential ease-out.
donts: Don't add a second accent hue, for any state.
Don't give an amber fill to any action other than Install.
Don't set running text in amber, or fill a large surface with it.
Don't set text in Stone at body sizes, or in Signal Amber at any size.
Don't use green or turquoise in imagery.
Don't let the page turn heavy or dark. The first screen of the front page is the one dark place; below it Basalt and Ocean surfaces stay small against the Mist.
Don't add landscape imagery beside the four photographs: no drawn landscape, no generated picture, no mirrored picture.
Don't blur a photograph, and do not show a blurred preview while it loads. Only a glass panel softens what lies behind it.
Don't reach for a veil before the placement of the picture and the colour of the text have been tried, and never lay one over a whole picture.
Don't move a photograph with the scroll.
Don't build a generic SaaS landing page: no centred headline over a gradient, no grid of icon cards, no wall of claims.
Don't put a label above any heading other than the two the mood board shows, and do not set a label in amber text.
Don't stack shadows or lift flat content. The glass shadow and the window shadow are the whole vocabulary.
